title: Set off and Carry Forward of Losses
outcomes: Apply inter-source and inter-head set-off rules.
Carry forward and set off losses by head.
Apply rules on amalgamation, succession and change in shareholding.

meta.exam_tip: Set off within the head first, then across heads, and show expiry years for carried-forward losses.

concepts.title: Inter-source and inter-head set-off
body: Section 108: a loss from one source can be set off against income from another source under the same head, except that long-term capital loss is set off only against LTCG, speculation loss only against speculation income, loss from specified businesses under section 46 only against such businesses, and loss from owning race horses only against that activity. Losses from exempt sources cannot be set off.
Section 109: a loss under one head may be set off against income under another head, but business loss cannot be set off against salary, and capital loss cannot be set off against any other head.

House property loss: outside the default regime, set off against other heads up to ₹2,00,000 a year (section 110); under the default regime of section 202, it cannot be set off against other heads at all.
concepts.analogy: Same head first, then other heads, subject to fences.
concepts.work: A long-term capital loss cannot absorb short-term gains.

concepts.title: Carry forward of losses by head
body: House property loss (section 110): carried forward 8 years, set off only against house property income. Capital loss (section 111): 8 years — short-term loss against any capital gain, long-term loss only against LTCG.

Business loss (section 112): 8 years against business income; the business need not continue. Speculation loss (section 113): 4 years against speculation income. Specified business loss under section 46 (section 114): indefinitely against specified business income. Race-horse loss (section 115): 4 years against that activity.

Unabsorbed depreciation (section 33(11)) is carried forward indefinitely and can be set off against any head other than salary. Order: current depreciation, brought-forward business loss, unabsorbed depreciation.
concepts.analogy: Eight years for most, four for speculation and race horses, no limit for depreciation.
concepts.work: A speculation loss of T.Y. 2026-27 expires after T.Y. 2030-31.

concepts.title: Losses on amalgamation, succession and change in shareholding
body: Section 116: on qualifying amalgamations (companies owning industrial undertakings, ships or hotels; banks with specified banks; PSUs; erstwhile PSUs after strategic disinvestment) and on specified business reorganisations, the amalgamating company's losses and unabsorbed depreciation pass to the successor. The amalgamating company must have carried on the business for 3 years and held three-fourths of its fixed assets for 2 years; the successor must hold three-fourths of those assets and continue the business for 5 years.

Carry forward in the successor's hands is restricted to the remaining part of the eight years counted from the year the loss was first computed for the original predecessor. Section 117 covers bank and government company amalgamations; section 118 cooperative banks.

Section 119: on change in constitution of a firm, the loss share of a retired or deceased partner (beyond his profit share) lapses; on succession other than by inheritance the successor cannot use the predecessor's loss; for a closely held company, losses carry forward only if persons holding at least 51% of voting power on the last day of the loss year continue to hold it — with relief for eligible start-ups (all original shareholders continue, within 10 years of incorporation), death, gifts to relatives and IBC resolutions.
concepts.analogy: Losses follow continuity of ownership or business.
concepts.work: A 75% common holding on both last days preserves the loss.

concepts.title: Return of loss and restrictions
body: Section 121: capital, business, speculation, specified business and race-horse losses can be carried forward only if determined in a return filed within the time under section 263(1).
House property loss and unabsorbed depreciation are not subject to this condition.
Section 120: income brought to tax as undisclosed after a search, requisition or survey cannot be reduced by any loss or unabsorbed depreciation.
concepts.analogy: File on time or lose most losses.
concepts.work: A belated return of business loss forfeits its carry-forward.

viva.q: Can house property loss be set off under the default regime?
viva.model: Inter-head set-off of house property loss is barred under the default regime of section 202.

viva.q: What is the order of set-off for business losses and depreciation?
viva.model: Current depreciation first, then brought-forward business loss, then unabsorbed depreciation.

viva.q: What happens to a retiring partner's share of loss?
viva.model: The portion of loss proportionate to his share, beyond his profit share, lapses for the firm.

viva.q: Can heirs use a deceased proprietor's business loss?
viva.model: Yes, succession by inheritance allows legal heirs, even as a firm, to set off the loss.

viva.q: Can losses be set off against undisclosed income found in a search?
viva.model: Section 120 bars it: neither losses nor unabsorbed depreciation may reduce income detected that way.
